match.reason: The closest bank point, Access to services, covers distance and travel to services in remote places but does not teach telehealth or online learning, which the new point requires, so adding them would change the card's content rather than make a small adjustment.

draft.title: Access to services and facilities
card: Services and facilities include schools, hospitals, shops and public transport. How close and easy they are to reach affects how liveable a place feels.
Access is about more than distance. Cost, travel time, opening hours and whether transport runs often also decide how easy a service is to use.
Remote places often have fewer services, and the ones they have can be a long way off. People there may travel far for a specialist or a larger shop.
Technology can help fill some gaps. Telehealth gives medical appointments by video call, and online learning lets students study when a school is far away.
draft.remember: Easy access to services makes a place more liveable. Remote places often use telehealth and online learning to help.

a.q: Which change would most improve access to services for a small town?
opts: A bus that runs to the regional hospital each day
A new park beside the town's main street
A mural painted on the local hall wall
A yearly street party for the whole town
a.why: A daily bus makes a hospital easier to reach, which improves access to a service. A park, mural or party may be enjoyable, but they do not make services easier to reach.
a.clue: Which option helps people reach a service?

b.q: Priya lives on a remote farm in north-west Victoria, 150 km from the nearest high school. Which option best helps her keep learning?
opts: Online learning, which she can do from home
Moving the school bell to a later time
Building more shops in a distant city
Planting trees around the farm house
b.why: Online learning lets Priya study without travelling the long distance to school, so it gives her access to the service. Shops in a distant city do not help her reach education.
b.clue: Which option brings the school to her, not her to the school?

a.best: A bus that runs to the regional hospital each day

b.best: Online learning, which she can do from home

problems.detail: The right option stands out. It is the only one with an explanatory clause ('which she can do from home'), and the distractors (moving the school bell, shops in a distant city, planting trees) are so implausible that a student can pick the answer without knowing the idea.
The right option is the longest and the only one with precise detail ('regional hospital', 'each day'), so it stands out slightly from the shorter distractors.

check.summary: The facts are correct and both intended answers are right. a.q: Which change would most improve access to services for a small town?
opts: A daily bus from the town to the nearest hospital
A new park with seats beside the main street
A yearly music festival held at the showgrounds
Fresh paint and murals on the old town hall
a.why: A daily bus makes the hospital easier to reach, so it improves access to a service. A park, festival or murals may make the town nicer, but none of them helps people reach schools, hospitals or shops.
a.clue: Which change helps people reach a service?

b.q: Priya lives on a remote farm in north-west Victoria, 150 km from the nearest high school. Which option would best let her study while living at home?
opts: Online classes she can join from her farm
Telehealth calls she can join from her farm
A bigger library at the school 150 km away
A new high school in a Melbourne suburb
b.why: Online learning brings classes to Priya, so she can study without the long trip. Telehealth uses the same kind of technology, but it gives medical appointments, not schooling. A bigger library or a new school far away does not make school any easier for her to reach.
b.clue: Which technology is for schooling rather than health?

a.best: A daily bus from the town to the nearest hospital
